A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Constrained Discrete Diffusion and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices. Their content can be reliably matched despite reformatting and section moves.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on toxicity mitigation, molecular generation, and instruction following, including hyperparameter ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds an entropy analysis of generated toxicity-task outputs.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects its continuation condition from violation below tolerance to violation above tolerance, and indexes the squared penalty by individual constraint. These are limited corrections to the stated algorithm; the underlying projection framework is retained, and an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: The toxicity, QM9 molecular accessibility/novelty, counting, and COLLIE lexical tasks retain their training and evaluation coverage. The added entropy analysis examines the existing toxicity application rather than a new dataset or scenario.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same autoregressive, PPLM, FUDGE, MDLM, UDLM, and diffusion-guidance comparators. The new entropy analysis compares CDD with its already evaluated MDLM base model.

E3.justification: v3 Appendix E adds per-sequence token-frequency entropy as a diversity metric at the existing toxicity thresholds. Previously documented model sizes, judges, generation settings, ablation protocols, and runtime procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new entropy analysis tests whether toxicity constraint enforcement reduces output diversity. Existing ALM hyperparameter, projection-frequency, and projection-start analyses are retained with unchanged evidence.

E5.justification: v3 Table 5 newly reports 95% confidence intervals for entropy. Existing perplexity uncertainty and runtime percentile reporting remain unchanged. No additional run counts, seeds, or confidence-interval construction procedure are disclosed.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds mean entropy of 5.577 for MDLM and 5.521, 5.519, and 5.544 for CDD at thresholds 0.25, 0.50, and 0.75, respectively, with decreases of 1.00%, 1.04%, and 0.59%. Earlier benchmark tables, ablation values, runtime results, and plotted findings are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1, its assumptions, and the Appendix F derivation are unchanged. Equation (2) makes the learned reverse-kernel notation and denoiser substitution explicit without changing the transition formula. The standard entropy formula documents the added evaluation metric.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of sampling-time constraint enforcement without generator retraining, zero violations across the studied tasks, and preserved sample quality. Entropy results support an existing diversity claim rather than introduce a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the small entropy decreases and reported confidence intervals as evidence that CDD preserves generative diversity. The model-scale and computational-overhead limitations are unchanged and merely move from Appendix A to Section 6.

D1.justification: The experimental-setup appendix moves from C to B while retaining surrogate-model details, ALM hyperparameters, tokenizers, tuning-data construction, and implementation-source instructions. Hardware disclosures and code/data access information are also retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Gruver et al.'s Protein Design with Guided Discrete Diffusion and distinguishes its hidden-state guidance from CDD's feasibility projection. Four general diffusion/image/video references disappear with the shortened background; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 removes the general continuous-diffusion overview, introduces numbered method subsections, moves limitations into the main text, and adds explanatory prose about prox-regularity. It also corrects typos and revises the author list and acknowledgments. Most existing narrative is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a document-wide NeurIPS layout with narrower text blocks, removed running headers, revised title/author arrangement, and restyled tables and pseudocode. Displays are resized and repositioned; the SA illustration moves into Appendix B and entropy Table 5 is added. Existing plot content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Algorithm 1's reversed continuation condition and adds direct entropy measurements with uncertainty reporting to support the previously asserted preservation of diversity. These improve clarity and evidential support, while the central experiments and proof remain unchanged. The gain is limited because the entropy confidence-interval calculation is not explained.
